findings: Hardcoded IP 192.0.2.2 and MAC 02:00:00:00:00:02 are taken directly from frozen literal frames; consistent with provided old oracles.
UDP frame extraction relies on case id 'latest-replaces' and step at_ms 2 in the UDP oracle; matches frozen udp oracle structure.
Ethernet wrapping pads TCP SYN frame to minimum 60 bytes as required by contract; checksum and padding match old core fixture.
Case4 does not explicitly assert intermediate L.control/PENDING and ip_pending_owner/UDP after TCP abort; final ARP reply behavior implicitly verifies preservation of UDP pending and query.
No import of copy/struct needed by the generated cases; use of built-in list/bytes is within allowed builtins.
limitations: Only the four contract-required scenarios are covered; no additional cases for multiple TCP retransmissions before ARP resolution, UDP failure after owner replacement, or ARP cache expiry during pending.
Assumes initial ARP cache empty and no pre-existing pending packet beyond steps; no test for cache hit on connect.
Does not explicitly verify that L.query is not rearmed when TCP connect overwrites UDP pending in case3; absence of tick after connect leaves this partially inferred.
Relies on exact frozen old-oracle frame bytes; any modification to those literals would invalidate expected outputs without warning.
